key_insight: Settling spheroids align under inertial torque, while turbulent gradients tilt them away, producing a lateral-slip maximum when alignment and Kolmogorov rates become comparable.
engineering_relevance: For known forcing statistics, a measured lateral-slip peak could constrain the inertial torque coefficient or turbulent dissipation rate.
method: Model overdamped orientation as random motion in a quadratic alignment potential.
Use an exact Boltzmann distribution for isotropic Gaussian white noise and a linear-response closure for correlated forcing.
Represent dissipation intermittency with a lognormal mixture of Boltzmann distributions.
evidence_signal: Tensor-forced simulations reproduce the nearly shape-independent slip-peak ratio, while the intermittent model captures plate-orientation distribution shapes from direct numerical simulations better than a single Boltzmann distribution.
watch_item: The finite-correlation closure is least accurate in the random-to-aligned crossover, and its rapid-settling limit assumes fixed-orientation forcing statistics.
paper_title: Orientation and slip statistics of spheroids settling in turbulence
